programs.name: Tabata 20/10 Cycling
programs.author: Izumi Tabata / Ritsumeikan University
programs.description: Eight 20-second efforts with 10-second recovery periods form the well-known four-minute Tabata block. GymClues adds a five-minute warm-up and five-minute cool-down. The original laboratory intensity was demanding; this app does not prescribe a universal resistance or promise the original study's results.
programs.schedule: Three sessions per seven-day cycle, with recovery days between. This four-week schedule is a GymClues scheduling choice, not a reproduction of a complete research study.
programs.progression: Keep the work/recovery timings. Begin only when ready for vigorous exercise; individualize effort and reduce intensity if control deteriorates. Do not increase speed, resistance and duration together.
programs.rest: Easy recovery between efforts; avoid stacking hard interval sessions on consecutive days.

programs.name: Norwegian 4×4 Intervals
programs.author: Cardiac Exercise Research Group / NTNU
programs.description: Four four-minute hard intervals separated by three minutes of active recovery, preceded by a ten-minute warm-up and followed by five minutes easy. This treadmill implementation uses running for hard efforts; brisk uphill walking is an option when it produces the intended effort with good control. Speeds and inclines must be individualized.
programs.schedule: Three sessions per seven-day cycle, with recovery days between. This four-week schedule is a GymClues scheduling choice, not a reproduction of a complete research study.
programs.progression: Keep the work/recovery timings. Begin only when ready for vigorous exercise; individualize effort and reduce intensity if control deteriorates. Do not increase speed, resistance and duration together.
programs.rest: Easy recovery between efforts; avoid stacking hard interval sessions on consecutive days.

programs.name: McMaster One-Minute Workout
programs.author: Martin Gibala and colleagues / McMaster University
programs.description: Three 20-second cycling sprints provide one minute of hard effort within a ten-minute session: two minutes easy to start, two minutes easy between sprints and three minutes easy to finish. This is sprint interval training, included here under HIIT. The study used supervised all-out cycling; a lower-intensity adaptation is not the identical research protocol.
programs.schedule: Three sessions per seven-day cycle, with recovery days between. This four-week schedule is a GymClues scheduling choice, not a reproduction of a complete research study.
programs.progression: Keep the work/recovery timings. Begin only when ready for vigorous exercise; individualize effort and reduce intensity if control deteriorates. Do not increase speed, resistance and duration together.
programs.rest: Easy recovery between efforts; avoid stacking hard interval sessions on consecutive days.
